Nigeria’s U-23 side, the Olympic Eagles, overturned their first-leg deficit with a commanding 4-0 victory over the Democratic Republic of Congo to reach the final qualifying round of next year’s U-23 Africa Cup of Nations, PUNCH Sports Extra reports. Having lost the first leg in Lubumbashi four days earlier, the Olympic Eagles responded emphatically at the Remo Stars Stadium in Ikenne-Remo, taking the lead in the eighth minute through Alex Oweilayefa. The forward tapped into an empty net after the Congolese goalkeeper spilled a fierce close-range effort from Umar Abubakar, with Nigeria having already missed a couple of chances before breaking the deadlock. The hosts maintained their attacking pressure, pinning the visitors back as Oweilayefa, Abubakar, Peter Osayande, Saleh Sadiq, Aderemi Adeoye and Wilfred George continued to threaten. Sadiq came close to doubling Nigeria’s lead in the 38th minute, but his effort was cleared off the line, while Abubakar missed from close range four minutes later as the Olympic Eagles continued to dominate. Add us to your Preferred Sources Nigeria resumed the second half with greater intensity, and their pressure paid off two minutes after the restart when Osayande finished from close range following good work down the left by Oweilayefa and Adeoye. The goal drew the tie level on aggregate, leaving the Olympic Eagles needing another to complete the turnaround. Osayande subsequently moved to the left flank, where his pace and direct running caused further problems for the Congolese defence. One of his attacking runs created the opportunity for substitute Victor Samuel to score Nigeria’s third, finishing from close range after the visitors failed to deal with the move. The Olympic Eagles sealed their passage in the third minute of added time when substitute Abdulmuiz Adeleke converted a penalty to complete the 4-0 victory and a 4-2 aggregate win. Nigeria will now face Zambia in the final qualifying round after the southern Africans edged Burkina Faso 3-2 on penalties following a 1-1 aggregate draw. Zambia and Burkina Faso had finished level over two legs before the former prevailed in the shootout to book their place in the final round.
